reasons: internal/manifest/lockfile.go:256-270 parsePipfileLock appends every entry of `default` and then of `develop` with no de-duplication, so a package resolved into both sections at the same version is emitted twice as a byte-identical Package. Verified by running ParseLock("Pipfile.lock", {"default":{"six":{"version":"==1.16.0"},...},"develop":{"six":{"version":"==1.16.0"},...}}) -> 4 packages with `six@1.16.0` appearing twice. This is the shape pipenv actually writes: it resolves the two sections independently and each carries its full transitive closure, so shared transitives (six, packaging, typing-extensions, urllib3, idna, attrs) land in both. Every other parser in this same file guards against exactly this with a `seen` map — parseGoSum:97-101, parsePackageLock:119-127, parseYarnLock:167,185-188, parsePnpmLock:215,224-228 — and the new one is the only parser that does not.

internal/indexer/indexer.go:633-637 is where that duplicate becomes a hard failure. The batch statement is `INSERT INTO repository_packages_staging(...) VALUES (...),(...) ON CONFLICT(generation_id,repository_id,ref_name,ecosystem,name,version,manifest_path) DO UPDATE SET scope=excluded.scope`, and the two duplicated rows are identical in all seven conflict-target columns (same manifest_path "Pipfile.lock", same ecosystem "pypi", same version) and land in the same 200-row batch (packageInsertBatch=200, indexer.go:1004). PostgreSQL — a first-class backend here (internal/store/store.go:12,47 pgx; internal/{app,backup,notification}/postgres_integration_test.go) — rejects a multi-row ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE that touches the same row twice with `ERROR: ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE command cannot affect row a second time`, and indexer.go:636-638 turns that into `return fail(err)`, aborting the entire index generation for the ref. Before this PR Pipfile.lock was ignored, so this is a new failure mode: on Postgres, indexing a repository that contains an ordinary Pipfile.lock now fails outright rather than gaining an inventory. SQLite applies the rows sequentially and silently collapses them, which is why `go test ./internal/indexer/ ./internal/manifest/` is green and hides this.

internal/manifest/lockfile_test.go:98-210 no case covers a package present in both `default` and `develop`, i.e. the single most common Pipfile.lock property, so the defect above is not exercised by any assertion. TestPipfileLockStatesTheVersionAlone (lockfile_test.go:203-209) uses a one-package `default` only and also cannot reach it.
notes: The rest of the change checks out. RecognizeLock/ParseLock is genuinely the only discovery path (indexer.go:524, 590, 746), manifest.Recognize() does not also claim these base names so appendPackages (indexer.go:1020) will not double-parse them, and docs/configuration.md:754-760 is the only live list of supported files (docs/release-notes-v0.52.4.md is historical and correctly untouched). No scope creep, no dependency or format churn, no auth/migration/secret/deletion logic touched.

The new tests do fail on pre-change code: RecognizeLock("uv.lock"/"pdm.lock"/"Pipfile.lock") returned ("", false) before, hitting t.Fatalf at lockfile_test.go:189. So item 1 of the checklist is satisfied for the uv/pdm paths.

The uv/PDM claim about column-zero anchoring is correct: lockName/lockVersion are `(?m)^name\s*=` with no leading-space allowance, and uv writes `dependencies = [` / `requires-dist = [` entries as indented `    { name = "x" }`, so they cannot supply a name. The `absent: ["certifi"]` assertion at lockfile_test.go:130 does test this for real.

Weak assertions, not a reject on their own: the Pipfile.lock `absent` list at lockfile_test.go:168 includes "_meta", "hash" and "sources", which are unreachable by construction since only the two named sets are walked — those three are tautologically true. Only "internal-lib" (the VCS-pinned entry) is a meaningful assertion in that list.

parsePipfileLock iterates Go maps, so its output order is nondeterministic across runs. That matters where the result is truncated — MaxLockPackages (lockfile.go:79-81) and maxPackagesPerRef (indexer.go:617-621) — because an oversized Pipfile.lock would contribute an arbitrarily different subset each index run. parsePackageLock has the same property already, so this is pre-existing rather than introduced.

Pipfile.lock `develop` packages are recorded with Scope "resolved" identically to `default`, so the dev/runtime distinction pipenv states is dropped. That matches how poetry.lock is already handled, so it is consistent — just flagging that the develop set now inflates the runtime inventory for pipenv repositories.
Reverting is trivial: the change is code and docs only, with no migration, no schema change and no external state written. A plain revert of 470ee9f restores prior behaviour exactly.
